content:
David J. DeBonis is a marketing strategist, science communicator, and writer. He writes about biomedical research at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus and runs an independent consulting practice, Antilo Design.
His earlier work includes e-commerce operations and product education at Nano Bella, teaching English language arts, and consulting with students at the CU Denver Writing Center.
Research and communication An interest in how people understand one another runs through David’s work. His language research examines how people learn; his science writing explains research to readers who may be unfamiliar with the field. In both, he pays attention to what the evidence supports and where questions remain.
Through Antilo Design, he works on marketing strategy and websites. Projects have included a brand transition for Colorado Sauce Company and local housing research for TGB Flooring. His selected work describes those projects alongside his scientific reporting.
Education and research David holds an M.S. in Marketing and a B.A. in English Writing, with a minor in Linguistics, from the University of Colorado Denver. His research experience includes language acquisition, phonetics, computational analysis, and writing pedagogy. More detail is available on the experience and education page.
Independent interests David founded Seeking Synthesis to write about health, science, adventure, and the human experience. He publishes research articles and personal essays there.
He also photographs landscapes and experiments with film. A small selection is in the photography gallery.

content:
Here are a few examples of my writing, consulting, and research.
Biomedical research communication University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus · Science communication
At CU Anschutz, I write about biomedical informatics, research software, and artificial intelligence. These articles cover uncertainty in health AI and software for studying biological images.
Can AI Say “I Don’t Know”? Understanding Uncertainty in AI — reporting on uncertainty in health AI. From Microscopes to Treatments: The Cytomining Ecosystem — an introduction to tools for studying biological images. Browse my CU Anschutz author archive.
A brand transition, carried into e-commerce Colorado Sauce Company · Through Antilo Design
For Colorado Sauce Company, I worked on a brand transition that included redesigned product labels and a move from Wix to Shopify. The work also covered product pages, email, and recipe content.
Read the Colorado Sauce Company case study.
Local research and useful content TGB Flooring · Through Antilo Design
For TGB Flooring, I developed company and project stories and content for the areas the business serves. I also compared 117 Highlands Ranch home listings for a research resource. The published findings explain the methods and limitations; an association in the listings does not establish cause and effect.
Read the TGB Flooring case study.
Product education and e-commerce operations Nano Bella · Director of E-Commerce Operations and Product Education
At Nano Bella, I led e-commerce operations and product education. My responsibilities included web development, direct-to-consumer marketing, email, and educational content about the products.
See role details and dates.
Research and computational projects Cafelytics · Python and data modeling
I supported the development of a computational simulation of a coffee operation, using data collected in Guatemala. Explore the Cafelytics repository.
Language acquisition · Research communication
My language research has included pronunciation and phoneme acquisition in students learning Spanish. View the research presentation.
Independent writing and photography I publish independent writing about health, science, adventure, and human experience at Seeking Synthesis.
Explore writing and publications or the photography gallery.
